sections.html:
Everett is the Snohomish County seat, so deed filings and tax questions land with the county, while permits stay with the city. Population is 113,567, up from 110,629 at the 2020 census.

Just 49.0 percent of homes are lived in by their owners. Many sellers are therefore landlords, heirs holding an inherited rental, or people with a basement or backyard unit. The sale route should follow the property: an empty inherited house, a duplex with tenants and a polished Rucker Hill home each need their own approach.

The median value of an owner-occupied home is $565,300. Treat that as a citywide midpoint. Your lot, street and repair needs will push your own number up or down.

Everett has 19 recognized neighborhood associations, and buyers shop by area. A few come up often:

  • Bayside and Port Gardner: downtown, the waterfront and the historic Rucker Hill residential area.
  • Northwest Everett and Riverside: older homes near Everett Community College, with historic districts in both.
  • Lowell: southeast of downtown and once its own town.
  • Silver Lake, Cascade View and Twin Creeks: south Everett, near Everett Mall and the lake.
  • Westmont: a mostly multifamily area in the southwest.

Everett Public Schools covers most of the city, but the southern and western neighborhoods belong to the Mukilteo School District. Check which one applies before a listing mentions schools.

The southwestern neighborhoods include creek ravines that drain to Port Gardner Bay, and the area is prone to mudslides. Owners of sloped or ravine-edge lots should dig out drainage and retaining wall records early.

sections.h2: Can I sell an Everett house that has an accessory dwelling unit?
sections.html:
Yes, and the city has relaxed its rules. Everett permits accessory dwelling units in all zones other than Light Industrial and Heavy Industrial. The city defines an ADU as a unit under 1,000 square feet that is subordinate to the main home, and each lot may hold two. A dwelling under 1,200 square feet needs no off-street car parking.

Fees matter to the next owner. Transportation impact fees are waived for one added ADU, school impact fees are waived for ADUs, and park impact fees are cut by half. In June 2026 the city also launched a gallery of pre-approved ADU designs, with a licensing fee of about $1,500.

  • If the unit was built without a permit, ask Everett Permit Services at PermitServices@everettwa.gov what it takes to legalize it before you list.
  • Basements and attics count as ADU space, garages do not, and each separate dwelling unit needs its own utilities.
  • In a historic overlay, any ADU that is not entirely inside the existing home goes to the Historical Commission.

sections.h2: Your choices if you need to sell fast
sections.html:
Three routes cover most Everett sales, and your deadline plus the state of the house should choose between them.

  • Agent listing: reaches the most buyers, though showings, inspections and loan contingencies can stretch the timeline by weeks.
  • Investor or cash buyer: you often pick the closing date and face fewer conditions, but the price tends to land under what a polished listing could bring.
  • For sale by owner: no listing commission, but pricing, disclosure forms and negotiating are yours.

Before signing with anyone, read the purchase agreement and ask to see proof of funds. Then set each offer next to your net after liens, taxes and loan payoff. The escrow company's closing officer can lay those figures out in a written estimate.

Every Washington sale carries a real estate excise tax, normally paid by the seller. RCW 82.45.060 builds the state share in steps. The first $525,000 of the price is taxed at 1.1 percent, the slice to $1,525,000 at 1.28 percent, the slice to $3,025,000 at 2.75 percent, and the rest at 3 percent. Starting with sales on January 1, 2027, the first step stretches to $551,000. A local rate rides on top of the state share, so the Snohomish County Treasurer or your escrow officer can give you the full number.

When title passes by deed, the treasurer receives the excise tax affidavit, the deed and the payment. Walk-in service at the excise tax counter runs Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., at 3000 Rockefeller, Everett, WA 98201.

The county splits the yearly property tax bill into April 30 and October 31 installments, and a mailed check needs a postmark on or before the day. An unpaid second half racks up interest and gets settled out of your proceeds at closing. The next first-half date is April 30, 2027.

Interest starts once a payment is late. RCW 84.56.020 sets 9 percent a year on overdue taxes for residential property of four units or fewer, with no extra penalties, while bigger or nonresidential parcels face 12 percent and penalties. Charges post on the first of every month. If the April 30 first-half payment is missed, the entire year's tax becomes delinquent.

Foreclosure becomes possible once taxes for a third delinquent year are owed in full. The county holds its Tax Lien Foreclosure Sale online and files the property list in court each May. An owner near that point can sell and have the back taxes paid from the proceeds at closing. State law also lets interest and penalties be waived in narrow cases, so ask the Treasurer's office if yours might qualify.

Having documents in hand before the first offer saves days. The usual sequence looks like this.

  • Insist that every offer is written down with price, closing date and the costs you would carry.
  • Learn how the buyer is paying and whether an inspection or a loan can undo the deal.
  • Request a lender payoff statement so the exact loan balance is known.
  • Collect permit papers for any basement, backyard unit or addition, and drainage papers if the lot slopes.
  • Ask escrow to add up excise tax, open property tax and other closing costs into one net figure.
  • Sign the deed and affidavit, then confirm the excise payment reaches the county treasurer.

A cash purchase has no lender appraisal or loan approval to wait on, so title work and your preferred move-out date drive the calendar. A listing adds showings, repair talks and the buyer's financing schedule.

faqs.q: How many people live in Everett, WA?
faqs.a: About 113,567 people lived here as of July 1, 2025, up from 110,629 in the 2020 census. No other Snohomish County city is bigger.

faqs.q: Who pays the real estate excise tax when an Everett house sells?
faqs.a: Usually the seller. When the seller skips it, the buyer inherits the responsibility and the unpaid amount can attach to the property as a lien. RCW 82.45.060 holds the state tiers, and a local rate is added.

faqs.q: Are accessory dwelling units allowed in Everett?
faqs.a: Yes. ADUs are allowed in every zone except Light Industrial and Heavy Industrial, with up to two per lot and a size cap of 1,000 square feet. Check the permit history of any existing unit before you sell.

faqs.q: When are Snohomish County property taxes due?
faqs.a: April 30 for the first half or the whole year, and October 31 for the second half. A mailed payment counts if its postmark is no later than the deadline.

faqs.q: Which school district serves my Everett house?
faqs.a: Everett Public Schools serves most of the city. The Mukilteo School District takes the southern and western neighborhoods, so verify your address first.
